answer: An applicant must bind its public key to one routing island: a single origin ASN and a covering IP prefix the registry will lease to only one seat. Entry is a spiral of five echo-timed probes: probe k equals H(epoch seed, pubkey, prior receipt) and may begin only after a public 12-minute beacon tick, so parallel hardware cannot precompute the path. At the summit tick the registry seats the first key that still uniquely holds that ASN and prefix. A colliding claimant, or a prefix already reserved, is evicted and its bond burned for two epochs.
